answer: In a Sybil-resistant mechanism, AI agents are assigned a unique identity based on their computational effort, similar to proof-of-work. To create an identity, an agent must solve a computational puzzle, analogous to extracting shale oil, requiring significant processing power and energy. The puzzle solution is then used to generate a digital pigment, serving as a unique identifier. As the tide of new agents attempting to join the network increases, the difficulty of the puzzle adjusts, making it costly for an attacker to create multiple fake identities, thereby preventing Sybil attacks.
